description:
bedrock-q67.21.16 makes a materializer refuse reads when the log's retention floor sits above where its data ends. It then stays unreadable for its lifetime. That was WRONG reasoning on my part (corrected with the user 2026-08-24) and this ticket fixes it.

THE HOLE IS FILLABLE. Restoring a snapshot at or above the retention floor and resuming the pull from there closes it exactly. The object-storage snapshot IS Bedrock's fetchKeys — not peer-to-peer like FDB's, but the same job: obtain a baseline you do not have. The startup path already does precisely this (Logic.maybe_load_snapshot/2 -> load_snapshot_from_object_storage/2). And in the case that matters most — bedrock-q67.21.17, where discovery reports a spurious :not_found — the snapshot exists and a retry simply succeeds.

WHY EXIT RATHER THAN REFETCH IN PLACE: a Bedrock materializer serves exactly ONE shard (State.shard_num/shard_id, singular), so a worker whose shard is unreadable is entirely useless. Exiting reuses machinery that already exists and is already damped — the distributor's DOWN handling retires the member and re-recruits with per-tag backoff — and the replacement re-runs discovery and restore through its ordinary startup path. No live database swap, no new retry loop.

FDB CANNOT DO THIS, and the asymmetry is the reason it has fetchKeys-in-place: an FDB storage server hosts MANY shards (storageserver.actor.cpp:470's per-shard state machine exists because one server holds a map of them), so killing the process over one unreadable range would take healthy ranges down with it. It must refetch in place. We hold one shard per worker, so worker replacement is the proportionate mechanism and the per-shard state machine collapses to a per-worker fact.

WHAT TO WATCH: the exit must be distinguishable from the existing voluntary exits so the distributor treats it correctly — {:shutdown, :idle} means 'do not re-recruit, revival is demand-driven' (bedrock-q67.21.5) and displacement means 'someone else owns this now'. An unreadable exit means the opposite: re-recruit promptly, because the shard needs coverage. Check the distributor's DOWN clauses before choosing the reason term.

ALSO: a replacement that hits the same condition (genuinely no snapshot, logs trimmed past the gap) will loop through recruit -> unreadable -> exit -> recruit. The distributor's per-tag backoff damps it, but the loop must be VISIBLE — this is a real data-availability failure, not a transient, and it should read as one in logs and telemetry rather than as churn.
title: An unreadable materializer exits so it can be replaced (the snapshot is our fetchKeys)
